# Import / Export evaluation

Status: in progress. Canonical observable contract: [CAPABILITY.md](capabilities/import-export/CAPABILITY.md).

## Cross-framework v1 contract

The dispatch packet dated2026-10-01 governs exact requester/scope, receipt/job transaction, CSV bounds/escaping, current permission, retry/reconciliation and explicit cleanup semantics. This track inspected only TanStack; no sibling repository was consulted. Native Start routes/server functions, existing pg-boss/Storage and application-owned registry preserve boundaries. Storage's optional GET/PUT/HEAD AbortSignal extension uses AWS SDK send and body destruction; no new storage protocol adapter.

## Upstream evidence

Rechecked at launch: [official csv-parse changelog](https://github.com/adaltas/node-csv/blob/master/packages/csv-parse/CHANGELOG.md) identifies7.0.3 on2026-09-25; [official stringify changelog](https://github.com/adaltas/node-csv/blob/master/packages/csv-stringify/CHANGELOG.md) identifies6.9.0. Both exact packages install with Bun1.4.2. [PostgreSQL18 isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/transaction-iso.html) and [timeouts](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-client.html) underpin the bounded snapshot/application transactions. [pg-boss12.35.0 supported API/types](https://github.com/timgit/pg-boss/blob/12.35.0/src/types.ts) supplies native retry metadata, cancellation, queue/id lookup and transactional Drizzle send. Existing pinned RustFS1.0.0/Garage2.4.1 fixtures are reused; no new provider account/infrastructure mutations on startup.

## Verification evidence

Bun1.4.2 frozen baseline install and targeted TypeScript pass. Seven CSV unit tests pass, including BOM/CRLF/quoted newline/quote, exact headers, fatal UTF8, byte/row/column/field/logical bounds, safe100-issue truncation, split UTF8 and formula vectors. Local HTTP cancellation fixture passes in Bun and Node24.19.0 for preabort/no I/O, GET acquisition/body destruction, PUT and HEAD acquisition.

Actual PostgreSQL18.1 + pg-boss12.35.0 and each real RustFS1.0.0/Garage2.4.1 pass the disposable transfer fixture: scoped/foreign visibility, UTF8/CSV, receipt idempotency conflict/replay, duplicate attempts/one committed apply, validation and SQL rollback, revoked permission before apply, durable cancel, source expiry/hash integrity, successful snapshot CSV/download and no pre-publication URL, artifact expiry, native missing-job reconciliation, scoped cursor, dry-run/explicit selected cleanup with retained receipt history. This fixture invokes worker core directly; it is not yet proof of process hard-crash or full production-worker behavior.

## Remaining completion gate

Generic clean-consumer install/runtime/removal/rebuild, all completed lifecycles, expanded race/deadline/crash/retry/snapshot fixtures, root/browser development+production, production image/explicit migrations/standalone worker/health and exact final-head hosted CI remain required. No done/ready/merge claim is made until those pass. Callback cooperative cancellation and customized consumer overlays must remain explicit limitations; source/package metadata is not runtime evidence.

## Additional checkpoint evidence

Root check passes331 tests with0 failures plus governance/lint/types/build; development browser suite passes12 cases including session/scoped transfer UI, safe expired source and durable cancellation without S3. Generic Import/Export clean installation, real two-provider runtime, removal/typecheck/rebuild passes with only Jobs/Storage closure. PostgreSQL deadline fixture closes active query I/O and rolls back on explicit abort; owned transactions do not replay writes.

Canonical Docker build and full completed-lifecycle run are blocked by anonymous Docker Hub HTTP429: oven/bun1.4.2 and Storage's required noooste/garage-ui:v0.13.0. Node24.21.0 Docker Official Image is available through official ECR mirror; host-built runtime image is supplementary evidence, not a passed canonical Dockerfile build. Hosted PR runs remain queued at the current checkpoint. These gates remain open; no verification requirement was weakened.

The application-owned personal Projects fixture passes on both providers with quoted name/null description content round-trip, fresh owner-bound IDs, other-owner exclusion, same-transaction Audit and header-only zero mutations. Native errors now set HTTP outcome status while retaining the safe serialized union; export UI preserves idempotency identity after ambiguous failures. Jobs producer imports are deferred to avoid entry-module cycles in both the reference and independent composition.

# Import / Export capability

Status: in progress. Optional (`defaultInstalled: false`); the root reference enables the personal Projects example. Evaluation: [IMPORT_EXPORT_MODULE_EVALUATION.md](../../IMPORT_EXPORT_MODULE_EVALUATION.md).

## Requirements and ownership

Hard capability requirements: Jobs and Object Storage. Baseline: PostgreSQL18, Drizzle, Node24; Authentication is application composition. Notifications and Audit Log are optional application-owned adapters, never imported into the independent capability. One application-owned typed registry declares at most64 definitions. Definition names match `[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[.-][a-z0-9]+)*`, maximum64; versions are bounded strings. Each definition supplies exact ordered columns, authoritative Zod schema, current scope authorization, transactional import and stable-key snapshot export callbacks. Unknown definitions fail invalid-input. Callbacks are trusted application code, must honor the supplied signal, and must not perform irreversible external I/O or independent commits.

## Cross-framework v1 contract

Trusted context contains `requesterId` and exact `{kind:'user'|'tenant',id}` scope. Identity IDs are nonempty opaque strings, maximum128 UTF16 code units, without controls; user scope must equal requester. Tenant selection is never authority. The application authenticates and verifies scope before constructing context; worker authorization resolves current permission from persisted requester/scope. Transfer UUIDs and UTC timestamps belong to the capability.

`createTransfers` injects one application-owned transaction adapter, registry, lazy Storage accessor, transaction-aware Jobs enqueue, supported Jobs lookup/cancel and optional same-transaction completion hook. `stageImport` authorizes, allocates a generated private source key/receipt, consumes bounded bytes, computes SHA256/length, uploads once and HEAD verifies length; its receipt and S3 PUT are separate operations. `startImport` owns a short transaction setting staged to pending and recording the exact queue/job ID; `requestExport` atomically creates pending receipt and enqueues only `{transferId}`. Caller idempotency keys are printable ASCII1–128, scoped by requester/scope/direction; fingerprints include definition/version and import receipt/source identity. Identical replay returns the existing receipt; changed request conflicts. There is no write retry after ambiguous connection loss.

States: uploading → staged → pending → succeeded/failed/cancelled. Pending includes queued/running; startedAt is descriptive, not a lease. `getTransfer` and newest-first `listTransfers` enforce exact requester/scope visibility; foreign resources return generic not-found. Summaries exclude object pointers, URLs, rows and job payloads. Lists default25, accept integer1–100 and canonical unpadded base64url `[1,createdAtISO,id]` cursor, maximum2048 characters, reapplying scope on every page. No cursor authorizes access.

`cancelTransfer` persists cancellation under the receipt lock before best-effort native Jobs cancellation. A committed success conflicts; cancellation never reverses domain data. A running locked import can win first. `getExportDownload` checks current permission, success and expiry before GET presigning for `min(600,remainingLifetime)`; under30 seconds is expired. Already issued bearer URLs can remain usable until expiry after revocation. Expiry denies access without physical deletion.

`reconcileTransfer` and bounded `reconcileTransfers` lock receipts and inspect only their recorded native queue/id through supported pg-boss APIs. Terminal receipt success always wins; native failed/cancelled becomes terminal failure/cancelled; missing native job becomes execution-lost. Active/retry/created are not failed based on elapsed time. Explicit operator command: `bun run import-export:operator -- reconcile <ids>`. Status refresh invokes reconciliation; no daemon is added.

`purgeTransferArtifacts(ids)` defaults dry-run, bounded100 selected receipts, terminal or expired abandoned uploading/staged only. Execute requires `bun run import-export:operator -- purge <ids> --execute`. It retains receipts, domain data and migrations; deletes only generated pointers recorded in selected receipts, including unpublished attempt output keys. No prefix deletion, startup cleanup or scheduled retention. Stop/drain in-flight attempts before execute; a provider PUT can finish after cancellation, so orphan cleanup can require another explicit pass after quiescence.

All bounded input validates before domain mutations. Import callback runs once per committed receipt under a row lock with fresh permission and deadline/state checks; callback domain writes and succeeded receipt share one Drizzle transaction. Concurrent stale attempts can parse but cannot apply a terminal receipt. This is one committed application, not exactly-once execution or business deduplication across transfers. Export uses one bounded read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction, stable application ordering and records snapshot time; successful attempt snapshot is not request time. After closing it, output uploads to a fresh generated key. A final row lock/current-permission/deadline check publishes pointer plus success. No download for partial output; retries may use a newer snapshot.

Attempt timeout includes configuration, resolution, body acquisition/transfer, validation, database and publication. Storage signal reaches SDK GET/PUT/HEAD and GET body destruction. PostgreSQL transaction_timeout/statement_timeout are at most min(30s,remaining budget), lock_timeout at most5s. No database transaction waits for S3/provider transfer. `createTransferTransactions` owns one disposable PostgreSQL Client connection per operation/transaction, closes that connection on deadline/claim cancellation and never destroys a shared application pool or retries writes; injected adapters must preserve this ownership/cancellation contract. Native queue policy:5 retries, initial30s, exponential backoff/native jitter, maximum900s, expiry timeout+30s, retention86400s. Only timeout/unavailable are advisory retryable. Known final native metadata permits final catch persistence; shutdown/claim abort does not imply terminal failure. Reconciliation handles hard crashes.

## CSV format and limits

Server-only pins `csv-parse:7.0.3`, `csv-stringify:6.9.0`; no umbrella/browser parser. UTF8 fatal decoding; optional BOM. Comma, double quotes/escaped quotes, LF/CRLF and quoted multiline. Mandatory exact ordered header; no duplicate, missing, unknown or prototype-related names. Rows parse as arrays before safe-object mapping. No dialect guessing, compression, workbooks, remote URLs, filename persistence, parser trimming or automatic type conversion. Empty data record invalid; one final terminator normal; header-only import succeeds with0 rows.

Fixed limits:64 columns; header64 UTF16 code units; field65536 UTF8 bytes; logical row262144 UTF8 bytes; normalized JSON at most twice max bytes;100 safe issues then errorsTruncated. Issues contain logical row ordinal(first data row1), registered field if available and closed invalid-value code, never cells/parser messages. Byte buffering is bounded and field/record/column checks precede parser allocation.

Exports registered order/header, CRLF/final CRLF, no BOM. Null/undefined empty, booleans true/false, finite numbers JS String; objects/arrays/nonfinite unsupported. Dates require explicit application ISO string formatting. Canonical string escaping prepends one apostrophe for leading =,+,-,@,TAB,CR,LF/fullwidth variants or whitespace then =,+,-,@/fullwidth variants; numeric negatives remain numeric. CSV deliberately changes dangerous strings and is not a lossless arbitrary-data backup. No mitigation guarantees every spreadsheet configuration is safe.

Server-only lazy settings: `IMPORT_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES` default16777216, integer1024–67108864; `IMPORT_EXPORT_MAX_ROWS` default10000,1–100000; `IMPORT_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` default60,5–300; `IMPORT_EXPORT_ARTIFACT_TTL_SECONDS` default86400,300–604800. Undefined/empty defaults; decimal digits only, no exponent/parseInt syntax. Existing DATABASE_URL/Jobs/Storage meanings remain. Missing S3 does not break build/start/health. TTL starts when staging/publication finishes; expired source cannot start/apply.

Safe static `{code,message,retryable}` errors: configuration,invalid-input,unauthenticated,forbidden,not-found,conflict,limit-exceeded,invalid-format,validation-failed,expired,cancelled,timeout,unavailable,execution-lost,unsupported,unknown. No raw causes, SQL, secrets, session objects, source cells, names, keys, URLs or environment values in default logs. Start transports return safe unions; upload HTTP statuses follow the documented outcome codes.

## Reference example

Personal Projects CSV is exactly `name,description`; existing trimmed name1–120/description0–1000 validator owns semantics, empty description null. Import creates fresh IDs/current owner, never accepts IDs or changes existing Projects. Export selects only personal owner Projects ordered createdAt ASC,id ASC. Reimport creates additional Projects: content round-trip, not restoration. Optional Audit composition belongs to the application. Native Start `/app/transfers` supports stage/start/status/safe issues/cancel/download and `/api/transfers-stage` accepts application-controlled bytes without browser key/scope/path/URL.

## Installation, migration and removal

Compile official source with `bun run add-ons:compile import-export`; generic catalog discovery supplies Jobs/Storage closure and official Drizzle integration. Independent assets provide an empty application registry to customize, never import unrelated capabilities. Overlay of the Jobs registry and drizzle.config is reviewed for the clean baseline only; customized consumers must manually preserve existing handlers/schema, not rely on generic semantic merging. Explicit application migration and Jobs migration are release prerequisites; no import/build/app/worker startup schema mutation.

Stop producers and drain or preserve pending work before removing handler/routes/UI/config/scripts/CSV packages. Retain Jobs/Storage and their packages/data, transfer schema declarations/tables, applied SQL/journal and objects. Explicit operator artifact purge is separate. Keep reusable authoring source separately if desired. See [removal recipe](../../docs/STARTING-A-PROJECT.md#remove-import-export).

## Verification and maintenance

`import-export:unit`, `import-export:compat`, `storage:abort`, generic `add-ons:test import-export`, all completed capability lifecycles, root check/browser development+production and image/explicit migrations/worker/health/exact-head hosted CI are completion gates. Two-provider fixtures create their own PostgreSQL database, S3 stacks and objects and use only disposable credentials. Status stays in progress until the entire gate passes. Evidence/remaining limits are recorded in the evaluation and PR, not inferred from source metadata.

files.src/integrations/import-export/schema.ts:
import {
	index,
	integer,
	jsonb,
	pgTable,
	text,
	timestamp,
	uniqueIndex,
	uuid,
	varchar,
} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
import type { TransferErrorCode, ValidationIssue } from "./validation";

const time = (name: string) =>
	timestamp(name, { withTimezone: true, precision: 3, mode: "date" });
export const transfers = pgTable(
	"import_export_transfer",
	{
		id: uuid("id").primaryKey(),
		requesterId: varchar("requester_id", { length: 128 }).notNull(),
		scopeKind: varchar("scope_kind", { length: 6 })
			.$type<"user" | "tenant">()
			.notNull(),
		scopeId: varchar("scope_id", { length: 128 }).notNull(),
		definition: varchar("definition", { length: 64 }).notNull(),
		version: varchar("version", { length: 64 }).notNull(),
		direction: varchar("direction", { length: 6 })
			.$type<"import" | "export">()
			.notNull(),
		status: varchar("status", { length: 12 })
			.$type<
				| "uploading"
				| "staged"
				| "pending"
				| "succeeded"
				| "failed"
				| "cancelled"
			>()
			.notNull(),
		createdAt: time("created_at").notNull(),
		updatedAt: time("updated_at").notNull(),
		startedAt: time("started_at"),
		completedAt: time("completed_at"),
		snapshotAt: time("snapshot_at"),
		artifactExpiresAt: time("artifact_expires_at"),
		idempotencyKey: varchar("idempotency_key", { length: 128 }),
		fingerprint: varchar("fingerprint", { length: 64 }),
		sourceHash: varchar("source_hash", { length: 64 }),
		sourceLength: integer("source_length"),
		sourceKey: text("source_key"),
		outputKey: text("output_key"),
		artifactKeys: jsonb("artifact_keys")
			.$type<string[]>()
			.default([])
			.notNull(),
		jobId: uuid("job_id"),
		jobQueue: varchar("job_queue", { length: 64 }),
		rowCount: integer("row_count"),
		byteCount: integer("byte_count"),
		errorCode: varchar("error_code", { length: 32 }).$type<TransferErrorCode>(),
		issues: jsonb("issues").$type<ValidationIssue[]>().default([]).notNull(),
		errorsTruncated: integer("errors_truncated").default(0).notNull(),
	},
	(t) => [
		uniqueIndex("transfer_request_key_idx").on(
			t.requesterId,
			t.scopeKind,
			t.scopeId,
			t.direction,
			t.idempotencyKey,
		),
		index("transfer_visibility_time_idx").on(
			t.requesterId,
			t.scopeKind,
			t.scopeId,
			t.createdAt.desc(),
			t.id.desc(),
		),
	],
);
export type Transfer = typeof transfers.$inferSelect;
